top_strength: Two things here are genuinely good. First, the rate framing is the correct one and better than what he used on his other call the same afternoon — "we charge $96 an hour per mover. So $192 for two" is per-mover, which is what the rubric asks for, and he disclosed the trip fee proactively and without apology before the hourly rate, explaining the why: "this location does have a, a travel fee only because it's a little outside of our free service zone. So there is, there is a $70 fee there that's just the flat fee." No surprises later. Second, the rapport was real and unforced — he caught that she was moving from Denver and ran with it ("You need to get warmed up, okay"), and she opened up about the weather back home. That is a warm, efficient six-minute intake.
coaching_note: He quoted a naked number and then folded on the objection in one sentence. Before the price, Celia heard no No Worries coverage, no Meet Your Mover, no On-Time Guarantee, no no-hidden-fees pitch, and no insurance explanation — so $550 arrived with nothing attached to justify it. When she said "I think that's just gonna be a little bit out of my price range more than I was expecting," the entire response was "Honest, yeah not a problem." No value reframe, no alternative, no ask. This is an unload-only, 25-box, one-bedroom job with elevator access right next to her unit — he had just said "it should be pretty quick to be honest," which is his own argument that she will likely pay the minimum and not the three-hour number that scared her. Say that back to her. Then give her the prep speech she actually needed: stage the trailer, take the small boxes up herself in a carload, and the 2.5-hour minimum is probably all she pays. At minimum, ask for the booking once — the email he sent was a booking ask ("just give us the go ahead") rather than the required review-and-correct verification ask, so he got neither the close nor the handoff credit.
phone_presence_notes: Genuine, unscripted rapport built off a detail he actually listened for — the Denver-to-Texas weather exchange got real reciprocation from her, and he stayed gracious when she declined — but held at 4 rather than 5 because he never used her name and the warmth disappeared the moment price came up.
